answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. In this architecture, a validator node perched on a network knoll issues a saffron credential token tied to unique hardware roots. An adversarial plume of fake bots faces exponential capital exhaustion: registration staking escalates superlinearly as cost(n) = k * 2^n, rendering swarm creation economically unviable.
